name: The Witches' Oak of Gragnano

location.address: Quercia delle Streghe, Via del Quercione, Gragnano / San Martino in Colle, Capannori

access: Free to see, at the end of a small signposted road from San Martino in Colle on the historic Villa Carrara estate, with parking on the dirt road in front. No source gives opening rules or the landowner, so check on arrival. Visitors have trampled the roots, so stay back from the trunk.
transport: About 10 km east of Lucca in Capannori, by road from Gragnano or San Martino in Colle. No public transport confirmed; plan on a car or bike.

photo_candidates.author: Guglielmo Giambartolomei
photo_candidates.why_this_trunk: Panorama named 'Quercia delle streghe', Gragnano, taken 2020-02-23; it is the photograph used on the tree's own Wikipedia article. No geotag on the file.

verify_notes: Register (MASAF 01/B648/LU/09, Regione Toscana list): downy oak, 400 cm girth, 15 m. Other sources give height 20 to 24 m and girth 4 to 4.5 m (dovealucca: 24 m, 4.5 m; Visit Tuscany: over 20 m, 4 m diameter, which is clearly circumference loosely stated; Wikipedia: 4 m). Age 'about 600 years' repeated by dovealucca, Wikipedia (citing La Stampa 2012 by Tiziano Fratus) and siviaggia (Jan 2026), no dendrological basis found, so kept broad and sourced. Pin: MASAF point 43.868061,10.648344 sits 13 m from Visit Tuscany's 43.868122,10.648505, so the spot is right but it is not a GPS fix at the trunk, hence approximate. Access is the soft point: the tree is on Villa Carrara's historic estate; every source treats it as a visitable attraction reached by a signposted road, none gives hours or a fee. Alive: siviaggia article of 2026-01-24 and Wikipedia photo of 2020-02-23 show it standing, siviaggia says condition fine. Damage history: vandals broke branches early 1900s, Nazis planned to fell it for firewood but villagers stopped it, struck by lightning in the 1960s, trunk hollow with nesting insects. Crown spread over 40 m, reaches second in Tuscany by size per Wikipedia. Overpass unreachable this pass; no OSM node checked.
facts_for_story: Crown spreads more than 40 m wide, growing horizontally, unusual for a downy oak (https://www.dovealucca.it/da-vedere/luoghi-naturalistici/129-la-grande-quercia)
Local legend says witches held sabbaths on its flat limbs, hence the name; locals also call it Quercione (https://siviaggia.it/posti-incredibili/quercia-delle-streghe-toscana/573147/)

Tradition links it to chapter 15 of Pinocchio where the Cat and the Fox hang the puppet from a great oak; Collodi's mother came from nearby Collodi (https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercia_delle_Streghe)
During the Second World War the occupying Germans marked it for firewood; villagers of San Martino in Colle stopped the plan (https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercia_delle_Streghe)

Struck by lightning in the 1960s; designated monumental by Regione Toscana at the request of the Comune di Capannori and WWF (https://www.dovealucca.it/da-vedere/luoghi-naturalistici/129-la-grande-quercia)
story:
This oak has had close calls. Vandals broke its branches in the early 1900s, lightning struck it in the 1960s, and its trunk is hollow and home to nesting insects. A wartime story, told without a source, says the villagers of San Martino in Colle talked occupying soldiers out of cutting it for firewood. It is still standing, by a January 2026 report in good condition.

What it saved is a crown more than 40 metres wide that grows sideways rather than up, unusual for a downy oak. Local legend says witches held their sabbaths on those flat limbs, which is where the name Quercia delle Streghe comes from; locals also just call it the Quercione, the big oak. Another tradition links it to chapter 15 of Pinocchio, where the Cat and the Fox hang the puppet from a great oak, since Carlo Collodi's mother came from nearby Collodi.

The usual age given is about 600 years, repeated by several sources but resting on no measurement, so treat it as an estimate somewhere between four and seven centuries. The register measures 4 metres round and 15 metres tall; other accounts give up to 24 metres. Regione Toscana declared it monumental at the request of the Comune of Capannori and WWF.

It stands on the historic Villa Carrara estate, at the end of a small signposted road. Tourists' feet have compacted its roots, so admire it from the fence.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the low, horizontal limbs spreading more than 40 metres, over a fenced ring of bare ground. It stands at the end of the small signposted road from San Martino in Colle, beside the lane.

best_time.label: winter, when the bare limbs show the full 40-metre spread

name: The Himalayan Cedar of Vinchiana

location.address: Piazzale of the Vinchiana cemetery, Via del Brennero Nord, Vinchiana, Lucca

access: Free and open at all times, at the side of the public forecourt in front of the village cemetery.
transport: About 8 km north of Lucca's walls on the Via del Brennero; no bus stop confirmed, so plan on a car or bike.
recognition_facts: It stands at the side of the open forecourt in front of the Vinchiana cemetery (RAMI field note)
About halfway up the trunk it divides into two large limbs (RAMI field note)
At 30 m it is a tall conifer in a village forecourt, so it is the obvious tree there; girth 518 cm at 130 cm height
verify_notes: MASAF 44/E715/LU/09 gives 530 cm and 30 m; RAMI (Il Registro degli Alberi, volunteer/technician field record) measured 518 cm at 1.30 m and 30 m on 2023-04-10, health 'good', accessibility 'accessible', relevance regional. Treated as two sources (MASAF list and an independent field record) though RAMI is probably derived from the same survey; flagged. Alive: 2023 survey only, lifecheck NONE, no photo found (no Commons file in 200 m, no iNaturalist record). Pin: RAMI 43.926564,10.521848 and MASAF 43.926575,10.521897 agree within 5 m, but both are register coordinates, so approximate; a forecourt tree is findable via location_site and the recognition facts. La Nazione's report on the updated Ministry list names a Himalayan cedar on Via del Brennero at Vinchiana (page not re-fetched, pointer only). No age source.
facts_for_story: Registered by Regione Toscana as a regional-relevance monumental tree; measured 518 cm girth and 30 m on 2023-04-10 (https://ilregistrodeglialberi.it/15377-cedro-del-cimitero-di-vinchiana-cedro-dellhimalaya-lucca-lu-toscana)
Surveyors call it 'a beautiful cedar' beside the cemetery forecourt of the Lucca hamlet, dividing into two big branches at half height (same page)
Deodar (Cedrus deodara) is a Himalayan species, planted in Italy as a 19th-century ornamental; no planting date known for this one
story:
Thirty metres of Himalayan cedar stand over the cemetery forecourt of Vinchiana, a hamlet about 8 kilometres north of Lucca's walls. When surveyors measured it on 10 April 2023 they found a trunk 5.18 metres round at chest height. The national register gives 5.30. Regione Toscana lists it as a monumental tree of regional importance, which puts a village forecourt on the same list as Tuscany's famous villa gardens.

The surveyors' note is short and plain. It calls the tree a beautiful cedar, standing at the side of the open forecourt, and records that about halfway up the trunk divides into two large limbs, which is the easiest thing to look for. They rated its health good and the site accessible.

The deodar is a Himalayan species, and Italy planted it as an ornamental in the 19th century. When this one went in, nobody has recorded. If you know who planted it, or remember the forecourt before the cedar was this tall, tell us.

There is nothing to book and no gate to pass. The forecourt is public and open at all times, on the Via del Brennero as it runs north out of Lucca. A car or a bike is the simplest way to get there, and a short stop is enough, though a cemetery asks for a quiet one.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by its height, about 30 metres, and the trunk that splits into two big limbs halfway up. It stands at the side of the open forecourt in front of the Vinchiana cemetery.
